## Project context
ATRIA-X: multi-tenant SaaS for home-care agencies. React19+Vite8+TS, Tailwind4, React Router 7, Clerk (auth/orgs), Convex (backend+DB), Vitest, Playwright. Formatting: 2-space indent, single quotes, NO semicolons, PascalCase components, camelCase utils. CORE RULE: a service is never billed unless its shift documentation is complete and approved (caregiver->coordinator->billing). Multi-tenancy is the central invariant: every Convex fn touching tenant data MUST go through authHelpers.ts guards (requireTenant / requireTenantRole / assertTenantDoc); enforce auth twice (RouteGuard + server). Roles: org:admin, org:coordinator, org:caregiver. After editing convex/* run `npx convex codegen`. Never edit convex/_generated by hand. Follow CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md.

## Task
Fix the live Clerk/Convex Phase 1 E2E failures so npm run e2e passes fully against the deployed Convex preview. Follow this exact process: reproduce the issue; think through possible causes; propose two solutions and choose the best; maintain/update the design doc at C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/live-e2e-fix-design-doc.md with stages and detailed to-do lists; implement conservatively and minimally using the existing project structure; add/adjust tests that prevent recurrence; deploy/sync Convex if seed/backend changes are needed; run lint, typecheck, unit tests, and full npm run e2e until all are green. Current repo already has uncommitted E2E/debugging changes from the parent Hermes session; treat them as a WIP baseline to inspect, keep only what is correct, and finish the root-cause fix. Known current failures: live e2e uses Clerk E2E users and deployed Convex at https://admired-mink-447.convex.cloud; geofence serial tests can see stale success/submitted state for Maya Torres; lifecycle can hit proof upload/autosave/review timing/state issues. Root-cause hypothesis to verify: seed/reset reuses deterministic shift IDs and leaves browser/Convex client stale state across serial scenarios; best solution may be to recreate fresh fixture shifts for each seed/reset, then redeploy Convex and rerun e2e. Do not skip gates. Do not claim success unless npm run e2e passes fully. Use Codex for planning/review and Kimi for implement/fix. Kimi CLI has been upgraded from 0.9.0 to 0.20.1; if Kimi-k2.7 is available use it, otherwise use the configured Kimi default and report that 2.7 could not be explicitly selected.

CORE RULE: a service is never billed unless its shift documentation is complete and approved (caregiver->coordinator->billing). Roles: org:admin, org:coordinator, org:caregiver. After editing convex/* run `npx convex codegen`. Never edit convex/_generated by hand. Follow CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md.

.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\fix_iter1.prompt.md:810:Observed failures after Convex deploy:
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\fix_iter1.prompt.md:811:1. Clerk login with password-created API users can trigger Clerk's new-device email factor, so browser-password sign-in is not deterministic.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\fix_iter1.prompt.md:812:2. Deployed Convex initially lacked `seed:seedE2E` / `seed:resetE2EShifts`; deploying fixed that.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\fix_iter1.prompt.md:813:3. Geofence tests were stateful/flaky after the first scenario because the same deterministic shift IDs carried cached submitted/success-screen state.

.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\fix_iter1.prompt.md:849:Solution B is the best fix: update E2E seed/reset behavior so each live E2E scenario starts from fresh fixture shift documents, while preserving the existing production app flow. Keep Clerk sign-in tickets for E2E auth only.

.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\review_codex_iter1.md:797:Observed failures after Convex deploy:
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\review_codex_iter1.md:798:1. Clerk login with password-created API users can trigger Clerk's new-device email factor, so browser-password sign-in is not deterministic.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\review_codex_iter1.md:799:2. Deployed Convex initially lacked `seed:seedE2E` / `seed:resetE2EShifts`; deploying fixed that.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\review_codex_iter1.md:800:3. Geofence tests were stateful/flaky after the first scenario because the same deterministic shift IDs carried cached submitted/success-screen state.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\review_codex_iter1.md:809:- The live Clerk flow requires either real email factor handling or backend sign-in tickets for deterministic automation.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\review_codex_iter1.md:813:### Solution A: Keep reusing deterministic fixture rows and add waits/reloads
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\review_codex_iter1.md:827:- Eliminates stale shift-detail cache by creating fresh shift documents for each reset/seed.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\review_codex_iter1.md:828:- Keeps tests representative of the real app while making fixture setup deterministic.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\review_codex_iter1.md:832:- Requires a conservative change in `convex/seed.ts` test fixture helpers and redeploy.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\review_codex_iter1.md:836:Solution B is the best fix: update E2E seed/reset behavior so each live E2E scenario starts from fresh fixture shift documents, while preserving the existing production app flow. Keep Clerk sign-in tickets for E2E auth only.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\review_codex_iter1.md:851:- Update `seed:seedE2E` / reset helpers so live E2E resets recreate fixture shifts or otherwise guarantee fresh state.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\review_codex_iter1.md:858:- Configure geofence in tests via deployed Convex mutation rather than relying only on UI timing.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\review_codex_iter1.md:871:- Run full `npm run e2e` until all 9 tests pass.

Formatting: 2-space indent, single quotes, NO semicolons, PascalCase components, camelCase utils. CORE RULE: a service is never billed unless its shift documentation is complete and approved (caregiver->coordinator->billing). Roles: org:admin, org:coordinator, org:caregiver. After editing convex/* run `npx convex codegen`. Never edit convex/_generated by hand. Follow CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md.

Do not skip gates. Do not claim success unless npm run e2e passes fully. Use Codex for planning/review and Kimi for implement/fix. .hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:590:Observed failures after Convex deploy:
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:591:1. Clerk login with password-created API users can trigger Clerk's new-device email factor, so browser-password sign-in is not deterministic.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:592:2. Deployed Convex initially lacked `seed:seedE2E` / `seed:resetE2EShifts`; deploying fixed that.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:593:3. Geofence tests were stateful/flaky after the first scenario because the same deterministic shift IDs carried cached submitted/success-screen state.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:602:- The live Clerk flow requires either real email factor handling or backend sign-in tickets for deterministic automation.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:606:### Solution A: Keep reusing deterministic fixture rows and add waits/reloads
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:620:- Eliminates stale shift-detail cache by creating fresh shift documents for each reset/seed.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:621:- Keeps tests representative of the real app while making fixture setup deterministic.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:625:- Requires a conservative change in `convex/seed.ts` test fixture helpers and redeploy.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:629:Solution B is the best fix: update E2E seed/reset behavior so each live E2E scenario starts from fresh fixture shift documents, while preserving the existing production app flow. Keep Clerk sign-in tickets for E2E auth only.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:644:- Update `seed:seedE2E` / reset helpers so live E2E resets recreate fixture shifts or otherwise guarantee fresh state.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:651:- Configure geofence in tests via deployed Convex mutation rather than relying only on UI timing.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:664:- Run full `npm run e2e` until all 9 tests pass.

.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:4233:.hermes-pipeline\20260623_153328\fix_iter1.prompt.md:4577:1. `submitDocumentation` still bypasses clock-out. The public mutation in [convex/shifts.ts](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/shifts.ts:563>) calls `submitShift`, which sets `status: 'submitted'` at line 237 after only checking for a clock-in punch. It never records `clockOutAt`, never inserts a `clock_out` punch, never enforces clock-out geofence, and never enqueues ADP sync. The existing UI still calls this mutation directly in [ShiftDocumentationForm.tsx](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/src/features/caregiver/components/ShiftDocumentationForm.tsx:70>). Route caregiver submission through `clockOut` or make direct submit reject unless the clock-out lifecycle has completed.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:4234:.hermes-pipeline\20260623_153328\fix_iter1.prompt.md:4579:2. `clockIn` can reopen completed or billable shifts. In [convex/shifts.ts](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/shifts.ts:619>), it checks only scheduled start time, then unconditionally patches `status: 'in_progress'` at line 644. A legacy `submitted`, `approved`, or `billing_ready` shift without a prior punch could be moved backward and get a new punch. Restrict clock-in to valid lifecycle states before mutating status.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:4235:.hermes-pipeline\20260623_153328\fix_iter1.prompt.md:4581:3. Public `timePunches.create` undermines the clock gate. [convex/timePunches.ts](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/timePunches.ts:20>) lets admins/coordinators insert clock punches directly at line 51 without geofence validation, audit, ADP scheduling, idempotency, or shift timestamp updates. Since note gating only checks whether a `clock_in` punch exists, this can satisfy the gate outside the official clock-in path. Remove it, make it internal, or harden it as an audited override with the same invariants.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:4236:.hermes-pipeline\20260623_153328\fix_iter1.prompt.md:4583:4. Required behavioral tests are missing. [convex/shiftClock.test.ts](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/shiftClock.test.ts:2>) mostly reads source files and asserts strings with `toContain` / `toMatch`, so it does not execute the mutations or prove the nine required scenarios. Add actual Convex mutation tests for note blocking, geofence missing/outside/inside, clock-out completeness, audit/punch side effects, and idempotent double clock-in.

.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:5106:.hermes-pipeline\20260623_153328\review_codex_iter1.md:4501:1. `submitDocumentation` still bypasses clock-out. The public mutation in [convex/shifts.ts](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/shifts.ts:563>) calls `submitShift`, which sets `status: 'submitted'` at line 237 after only checking for a clock-in punch. It never records `clockOutAt`, never inserts a `clock_out` punch, never enforces clock-out geofence, and never enqueues ADP sync. The existing UI still calls this mutation directly in [ShiftDocumentationForm.tsx](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/src/features/caregiver/components/ShiftDocumentationForm.tsx:70>). Route caregiver submission through `clockOut` or make direct submit reject unless the clock-out lifecycle has completed.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:5107:.hermes-pipeline\20260623_153328\review_codex_iter1.md:4503:2. `clockIn` can reopen completed or billable shifts. In [convex/shifts.ts](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/shifts.ts:619>), it checks only scheduled start time, then unconditionally patches `status: 'in_progress'` at line 644. A legacy `submitted`, `approved`, or `billing_ready` shift without a prior punch could be moved backward and get a new punch. Restrict clock-in to valid lifecycle states before mutating status.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\implement.prompt.md:5108:.hermes-pipeline\20260623_153328\review_codex_iter1.md:4505:3. Public `timePunches.create` undermines the clock gate. [convex/timePunches.ts](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/timePunches.ts:20>) lets admins/coordinators insert clock punches directly at line 51 without geofence validation, audit, ADP scheduling, idempotency, or shift timestamp updates. Since note gating only checks whether a `clock_in` punch exists, this can satisfy the gate outside the official clock-in path. Remove it, make it internal, or harden it as an audited override with the same invariants.

.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:30:ATRIA-X: multi-tenant SaaS for home-care agencies. React19+Vite8+TS, Tailwind4, React Router 7, Clerk (auth/orgs), Convex (backend+DB), Vitest, Playwright. Formatting: 2-space indent, single quotes, NO semicolons, PascalCase components, camelCase utils. CORE RULE: a service is never billed unless its shift documentation is complete and approved (caregiver->coordinator->billing). Multi-tenancy is the central invariant: every Convex fn touching tenant data MUST go through authHelpers.ts guards (requireTenant / requireTenantRole / assertTenantDoc); enforce auth twice (RouteGuard + server). Roles: org:admin, org:coordinator, org:caregiver. After editing convex/* run `npx convex codegen`. Never edit convex/_generated by hand. Follow CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md.

.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:580:Observed failures after Convex deploy:
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:581:1. Clerk login with password-created API users can trigger Clerk's new-device email factor, so browser-password sign-in is not deterministic.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:582:2. Deployed Convex initially lacked `seed:seedE2E` / `seed:resetE2EShifts`; deploying fixed that.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:583:3. Geofence tests were stateful/flaky after the first scenario because the same deterministic shift IDs carried cached submitted/success-screen state.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:592:- The live Clerk flow requires either real email factor handling or backend sign-in tickets for deterministic automation.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:596:### Solution A: Keep reusing deterministic fixture rows and add waits/reloads
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:610:- Eliminates stale shift-detail cache by creating fresh shift documents for each reset/seed.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:611:- Keeps tests representative of the real app while making fixture setup deterministic.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:615:- Requires a conservative change in `convex/seed.ts` test fixture helpers and redeploy.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:619:Solution B is the best fix: update E2E seed/reset behavior so each live E2E scenario starts from fresh fixture shift documents, while preserving the existing production app flow. Keep Clerk sign-in tickets for E2E auth only.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:634:- Update `seed:seedE2E` / reset helpers so live E2E resets recreate fixture shifts or otherwise guarantee fresh state.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:641:- Configure geofence in tests via deployed Convex mutation rather than relying only on UI timing.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:654:- Run full `npm run e2e` until all 9 tests pass.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:658:Stages 1 and parts of Stage 3 were implemented locally. Convex deploy succeeded earlier, but the remaining fixture-isolation change is not complete/deployed yet. Full E2E is still red at the time this doc was written.

.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:4223:.hermes-pipeline\20260623_153328\fix_iter1.prompt.md:4577:1. `submitDocumentation` still bypasses clock-out. The public mutation in [convex/shifts.ts](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/shifts.ts:563>) calls `submitShift`, which sets `status: 'submitted'` at line 237 after only checking for a clock-in punch. It never records `clockOutAt`, never inserts a `clock_out` punch, never enforces clock-out geofence, and never enqueues ADP sync. The existing UI still calls this mutation directly in [ShiftDocumentationForm.tsx](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/src/features/caregiver/components/ShiftDocumentationForm.tsx:70>). Route caregiver submission through `clockOut` or make direct submit reject unless the clock-out lifecycle has completed.

.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:5096:.hermes-pipeline\20260623_153328\review_codex_iter1.md:4501:1. `submitDocumentation` still bypasses clock-out. The public mutation in [convex/shifts.ts](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/shifts.ts:563>) calls `submitShift`, which sets `status: 'submitted'` at line 237 after only checking for a clock-in punch. It never records `clockOutAt`, never inserts a `clock_out` punch, never enforces clock-out geofence, and never enqueues ADP sync. The existing UI still calls this mutation directly in [ShiftDocumentationForm.tsx](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/src/features/caregiver/components/ShiftDocumentationForm.tsx:70>). Route caregiver submission through `clockOut` or make direct submit reject unless the clock-out lifecycle has completed.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:5097:.hermes-pipeline\20260623_153328\review_codex_iter1.md:4503:2. `clockIn` can reopen completed or billable shifts. In [convex/shifts.ts](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/shifts.ts:619>), it checks only scheduled start time, then unconditionally patches `status: 'in_progress'` at line 644. A legacy `submitted`, `approved`, or `billing_ready` shift without a prior punch could be moved backward and get a new punch. Restrict clock-in to valid lifecycle states before mutating status.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:5098:.hermes-pipeline\20260623_153328\review_codex_iter1.md:4505:3. Public `timePunches.create` undermines the clock gate. [convex/timePunches.ts](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/timePunches.ts:20>) lets admins/coordinators insert clock punches directly at line 51 without geofence validation, audit, ADP scheduling, idempotency, or shift timestamp updates. Since note gating only checks whether a `clock_in` punch exists, this can satisfy the gate outside the official clock-in path. Remove it, make it internal, or harden it as an audited override with the same invariants.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_231328\plan_final.md:5099:.hermes-pipeline\20260623_153328\review_codex_iter1.md:4507:4. Required behavioral tests are missing. [convex/shiftClock.test.ts](<C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/shiftClock.test.ts:2>) mostly reads source files and asserts strings with `toContain` / `toMatch`, so it does not execute the mutations or prove the nine required scenarios. Add actual Convex mutation tests for note blocking, geofence missing/outside/inside, clock-out completeness, audit/punch side effects, and idempotent double clock-in.

# ATRIA-X live Clerk/Convex E2E fix design doc

## Reproduction

Command:

```bash
npm run e2e
```

Environment:
- Clerk E2E users configured in `.env.local` / `C:\Users\pinol\.atriax\clerk-e2e.env`.
- Convex preview deployed at `https://admired-mink-447.convex.cloud`.

Observed failures after Convex deploy:
1. Clerk login with password-created API users can trigger Clerk's new-device email factor, so browser-password sign-in is not deterministic.
2. Deployed Convex initially lacked `seed:seedE2E` / `seed:resetE2EShifts`; deploying fixed that.
3. Geofence tests were stateful/flaky after the first scenario because the same deterministic shift IDs carried cached submitted/success-screen state.
4. Lifecycle test reached coordinator review but could time out on loading/filter state and proof-upload/autosave state.

## Root-cause analysis

The remaining issue is not missing Clerk credentials anymore. The root causes are:

- E2E fixture reset is not isolated strongly enough for a live Convex/browser run. Resetting the same existing shift documents in place leaves the browser/Convex client able to observe stale details for the same shift IDs after prior test scenarios.
- The tests depend on UI-driven geofence settings and role switching in the same page, which adds Clerk/Convex timing races.
- The live Clerk flow requires either real email factor handling or backend sign-in tickets for deterministic automation.

### Final confirmed root cause

`seed:seedE2E` (and the older `seed:resetE2EShifts`) locate the fixture shifts by their fixed `scheduledStart` timestamps and then patch the same documents back to a clean state. Because Convex document `_id`s stay identical across resets, the React/Convex client can reuse cached query results and component state keyed by those `_id`s. In the serial geofence and lifecycle suites this causes:

- `ShiftDocumentationForm` rendered for the same `shiftId` may briefly show the previous test's wizard step / autosaved values / success screen.
- `CaregiverTodayPage` and `CoordinatorReviewPage` may render stale status badges or filters before the reset mutations propagate through the live sync channel.
- Browser geolocation permission and `tenantSettings` cache can retain the previous scenario's values because the setting document is also patched in place.

The failures are intermittent because network timing and Convex subscription updates sometimes win the race, but the deterministic IDs make the race possible on every run.

## Possible solutions

### Solution A: Keep reusing deterministic fixture rows and add waits/reloads

Approach:
- Keep `seed:seedE2E` idempotent by patching the existing fixture shifts.
- Add explicit `page.reload()`, `await expect(...).toHaveAttribute('data-shift-status', 'scheduled')`, and longer timeouts in every test that follows a reset.
- Force a hard browser context reset between serial scenarios.

Pros:
- Smallest code diff in the backend.
- No Convex redeploy needed if only tests change.

Cons:
- Still vulnerable to stale query cache for the same shift IDs; waits only push the race around.
- Requires scattered, hard-to-maintain sleeps and reloads in every serial test.
- Already showed inconsistent behavior across serial tests.
- Does not fix the underlying client-state/keying problem.

### Solution B: Make live E2E fixtures isolated per reset by recreating shift documents

Approach:
- Change `seed:seedE2E` to delete the existing fixture shifts (and their child records) and insert brand-new shift documents on every reset.
- Keep the same `scheduledStart`, clients, and caregiver so tests can still locate shifts by name/time, but give each reset a fresh `_id`.
- Make `seed:resetE2EShifts` delegate to the same recreate logic so both mutation paths are isolated.
- Add a regression test that calls `seed:seedE2E` twice and asserts the returned `lifecycleShiftId` and `geofenceShiftId` are different.

Pros:
- Eliminates stale shift-detail cache by creating fresh shift documents for each reset/seed.
- Keeps tests representative of the real app while making fixture setup deterministic.
- Cleaner root-cause fix than adding waits everywhere.
- Confined to `convex/seed.ts` and one regression test; minimal surface area.

Cons:
- Requires a conservative change in `convex/seed.ts` test fixture helpers and redeploy.
- Slightly more delete/insert work on each reset (still tiny for two fixture shifts).

## Chosen solution

Solution B is the best fix: update E2E seed/reset behavior so each live E2E scenario starts from fresh fixture shift documents, while preserving the existing production app flow. Keep Clerk sign-in tickets for E2E auth only.

## Implementation stages

### Stage 1 â€” Auth determinism

To-do:
- Use Clerk Backend API sign-in tickets when `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` is available.
- Keep browser password fallback for environments without the secret key.
- Clear Clerk session/local storage/cookies between role switches.
- Assert E2E credential presence and fail loudly.
- Handle the ATRIA-X agency picker after Clerk organization selection.

Status: already implemented in `tests/e2e/helpers/auth.ts`. Keep as-is.

### Stage 2 â€” Fixture isolation

To-do:
- Refactor `seed:seedE2E` in `convex/seed.ts` to delete existing lifecycle/geofence fixture shifts and child records, then insert fresh shifts.
- Preserve fixture metadata (`scheduledStart`, clients `Sam Lee` and `Maya Torres`, caregiver assignment, default geofence disabled).
- Make `seed:resetE2EShifts` call the same recreate path so both entry points produce fresh IDs.
- Remove the temporary debug-only `lifecycleStatus` / `geofenceStatus` return fields added during debugging.
- Add return fields that expose the newly created shift IDs and a stable `status: 'seeded'` contract.

### Stage 3 â€” Test robustness

To-do:
- Configure geofence in tests via deployed Convex mutation rather than relying only on UI timing.
- Use scoped locators around the target shift card/section.
- Add GPS `accuracy` to Playwright geolocation mocks.
- Use returned/approved filters explicitly in coordinator review assertions.
- Increase Playwright timeout for live Clerk/Convex runs.
- Add a regression test verifying that two consecutive `seed:seedE2E` calls produce different shift IDs.

Status: most test-level hardening already implemented; remaining work is the fixture-isolation regression test.

### Stage 4 â€” Verification

To-do:
- Deploy Convex preview with seed fixes (`npx convex dev` or `npx convex deploy` against the preview project).
- Run `npm run lint`.
- Run `npm run typecheck`.
- Run `npm run test`.
- Run full `npm run e2e` until all 9 tests pass reliably (at least two consecutive full runs).

## Implementation notes

- The backend root-cause fix is intentionally limited to `convex/seed.ts` and `convex/seed.test.ts`. No production auth bypass, no unrelated refactors.
- The existing WIP improvements (Badge prop forwarding, ShiftNoteStep testid wrapper, env-file e2e script, scoped locators, Clerk ticket auth, Playwright timeout) are preserved because they are correct and reduce flakiness.
- After the fixture isolation change, every serial test starts with shift IDs the frontend has never seen, so stale component/query state is impossible regardless of browser caching.

## Final verification

Completed after deploying the seed fix to the Convex preview at `https://admired-mink-447.convex.cloud`:

- `npm run lint`: PASS
- `npm run typecheck`: PASS
- `npm run test`: PASS â€” 37 files, 289 tests
- `npm run build`: PASS, with the pre-existing Vite CSS optimizer warning for `.text-[var(...)]`
- `npm run e2e`: PASS â€” 9 Playwright tests, live Clerk users, deployed Convex preview

# ATRIA-X live Clerk/Convex E2E fix design doc

## Reproduction

Command:

```bash
npm run e2e
```

Environment:
- Clerk E2E users configured in `.env.local` / `C:\Users\pinol\.atriax\clerk-e2e.env`.
- Convex preview deployed at `https://admired-mink-447.convex.cloud`.

Observed failures after Convex deploy:
1. Clerk login with password-created API users can trigger Clerk's new-device email factor, so browser-password sign-in is not deterministic.
2. Deployed Convex initially lacked `seed:seedE2E` / `seed:resetE2EShifts`; deploying fixed that.
3. Geofence tests were stateful/flaky after the first scenario because the same deterministic shift IDs carried cached submitted/success-screen state.
4. Lifecycle test reached coordinator review but could time out on loading/filter state and proof-upload/autosave state.

## Root-cause analysis

The remaining issue is not missing Clerk credentials anymore. The root causes are:

- E2E fixture reset is not isolated strongly enough for a live Convex/browser run. Resetting the same existing shift documents in place leaves the browser/Convex client able to observe stale details for the same shift IDs after prior test scenarios.
- The tests depend on UI-driven geofence settings and role switching in the same page, which adds Clerk/Convex timing races.
- The live Clerk flow requires either real email factor handling or backend sign-in tickets for deterministic automation.

## Possible solutions

### Solution A: Keep reusing deterministic fixture rows and add waits/reloads

Pros:
- Smallest code diff.
- No backend fixture changes.

Cons:
- Still vulnerable to stale query cache for the same shift IDs.
- Requires scattered waits/reloads.
- Already showed inconsistent behavior across serial tests.

### Solution B: Make live E2E fixtures isolated per run/reset

Pros:
- Eliminates stale shift-detail cache by creating fresh shift documents for each reset/seed.
- Keeps tests representative of the real app while making fixture setup deterministic.
- Cleaner root-cause fix than adding waits everywhere.

Cons:
- Requires a conservative change in `convex/seed.ts` test fixture helpers and redeploy.

## Chosen solution

Solution B is the best fix: update E2E seed/reset behavior so each live E2E scenario starts from fresh fixture shift documents, while preserving the existing production app flow. Keep Clerk sign-in tickets for E2E auth only.

## Implementation stages

### Stage 1 Ã¢â‚¬â€ Auth determinism

To-do:
- Use Clerk Backend API sign-in tickets when `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` is available.
- Keep browser password fallback for environments without the secret key.
- Clear Clerk session/local storage/cookies between role switches.
- Assert E2E credential presence and fail loudly.

### Stage 2 Ã¢â‚¬â€ Fixture determinism

To-do:
- Update `seed:seedE2E` / reset helpers so live E2E resets recreate fixture shifts or otherwise guarantee fresh state.
- Ensure geofence settings default off after reset.
- Ensure lifecycle and geofence fixture shifts are scheduled/past and assigned to the E2E caregiver.

### Stage 3 Ã¢â‚¬â€ Test robustness

To-do:
- Configure geofence in tests via deployed Convex mutation rather than relying only on UI timing.
- Use scoped locators around the target shift card/section.
- Add GPS `accuracy` to Playwright geolocation mocks.
- Use returned/approved filters explicitly in coordinator review assertions.
- Increase Playwright timeout for live Clerk/Convex runs.

### Stage 4 Ã¢â‚¬â€ Verification

To-do:
- Deploy Convex preview with current seed fixes.
- Run `npm run lint`.
- Run `npm run typecheck`.
- Run `npm run test`.
- Run full `npm run e2e` until all 9 tests pass.

## Current status

Stages 1 and parts of Stage 3 were implemented locally. Convex deploy succeeded earlier, but the remaining fixture-isolation change is not complete/deployed yet. Full E2E is still red at the time this doc was written.

54: async function findClerkUserId(email: string): Promise<string> {
55:   const secretKey = process.env.CLERK_SECRET_KEY
56:   if (!secretKey) {
57:     throw new Error('CLERK_SECRET_KEY is required for live Clerk E2E user lookup.')
58:   }
59: 
60:   const usersResponse = await fetch(
61:     `https://api.clerk.com/v1/users?query=${encodeURIComponent(email)}`,
62:     { headers: clerkApiHeaders(secretKey) },
63:   )
64: 
65:   if (!usersResponse.ok) {
66:     throw new Error(
67:       `Could not look up Clerk E2E user ${email}: ${usersResponse.status}`,
68:     )
69:   }
70: 
71:   const users = (await usersResponse.json()) as ClerkUser[]
72:   const normalized = email.toLowerCase()
73:   const user = users.find((candidate) =>
74:     candidate.email_addresses.some(
75:       (entry) => entry.email_address.toLowerCase() === normalized,
76:     ),
77:   )
78:   if (!user) {
79:     throw new Error(`Clerk E2E user ${email} was not found.`)
80:   }
81:   return user.id
82: }

84: async function createSignInTicket(email: string): Promise<string | null> {
85:   const secretKey = process.env.CLERK_SECRET_KEY
86:   if (!secretKey) return null
87: 
88:   const tokenResponse = await fetch('https://api.clerk.com/v1/sign_in_tokens', {
89:     method: 'POST',
90:     headers: clerkApiHeaders(secretKey),
91:     body: JSON.stringify({
92:       user_id: await findClerkUserId(email),
93:       expires_in_seconds: 600,
94:     }),
95:   })
96: 
97:   if (!tokenResponse.ok) {
98:     throw new Error(
99:       `Could not create Clerk E2E sign-in ticket for ${email}: ${tokenResponse.status}`,
100:     )
101:   }
102: 
103:   const signInToken = (await tokenResponse.json()) as ClerkSignInToken
104:   return signInToken.token
105: }

225:   return page.evaluate(async () => {
226:     const clerk = (window as unknown as Record<string, unknown>).Clerk as
227:       | { session?: { getToken: () => Promise<string | null> } }
228:       | undefined
229:     const sessionToken = await clerk?.session?.getToken()
230:     if (sessionToken) return sessionToken

232:     const keys = ['__clerk_client_jwt', '__session', '__clerk_session_jwt']
233:     for (const key of keys) {
234:       const value = localStorage.getItem(key)
235:       if (value) return value

237:     return null
238:   })
239: }

69: async function extractClerkToken(page: import('@playwright/test').Page): Promise<string | null> {
70:   return page.evaluate(async () => {
71:     const clerk = (window as unknown as Record<string, unknown>).Clerk as
72:       | { session?: { getToken: () => Promise<string | null> } }
73:       | undefined
74:     const sessionToken = await clerk?.session?.getToken()
75:     if (sessionToken) return sessionToken
76: 
77:     const keys = ['__clerk_client_jwt', '__session', '__clerk_session_jwt']
78:     for (const key of keys) {
79:       const value = localStorage.getItem(key)
80:       if (value) return value
81:     }
82:     return null
83:   })
84: }

86: export default async function globalSetup(config: FullConfig) {
87:   if (!e2eCredentialsAvailable()) {
88:     console.log('E2E credentials not configured; skipping global seed.')
89:     return
90:   }
91: 
92:   const browser = await chromium.launch()
93:   const page = await browser.newPage({
94:     baseURL: config.projects[0]?.use.baseURL,
95:   })
96: 
97:   try {
98:     const roles: Record<string, RoleCredentials> = {
99:       admin: { email: E2E_ADMIN_EMAIL, password: E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD },
100:       coordinator: { email: E2E_COORDINATOR_EMAIL, password: E2E_COORDINATOR_PASSWORD },
101:       caregiver: { email: E2E_CAREGIVER_EMAIL, password: E2E_CAREGIVER_PASSWORD },
102:     }
103: 
104:     const userIds: Record<string, string> = {}
105:     for (const [role, credentials] of Object.entries(roles)) {
106:       await signInWithClerk(page, credentials.email, credentials.password, E2E_ORG_ID)
107:       const userId = await extractClerkUserId(page)
108:       if (!userId) {
109:         throw new Error(`Could not extract Clerk user id for ${role}.`)
110:       }
111:       userIds[role] = userId
112:       await signOut(page)
113:     }
114: 
115:     // Sign back in as admin so we can call the seed mutation with an admin token.
116:     await signInWithClerk(page, E2E_ADMIN_EMAIL, E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD, E2E_ORG_ID)
117: 
118:     // Bootstrap the tenant if this is the first run against this org.
119:     await page.goto('/select-agency')
120:     await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')
121: 
122:     const token = await extractClerkToken(page)
123:     if (!token) {
124:       throw new Error('Could not extract Clerk session token; cannot seed e2e fixtures.')
125:     }
126: 
127:     await seedE2EFixtures(token, {
128:       adminUserId: userIds.admin,
129:       coordinatorUserId: userIds.coordinator,
130:       caregiverUserId: userIds.caregiver,
131:     })
132:   } finally {
133:     await browser.close()
134:   }
135: }

1: # ATRIA-X live Clerk/Convex E2E fix design doc
2: 
3: ## Reproduction
4: 
5: Command:
6: 
7: ```bash
8: npm run e2e
9: ```
10: 
11: Environment:
12: - Clerk E2E users configured in `.env.local` / `C:\Users\pinol\.atriax\clerk-e2e.env`.
13: - Convex preview deployed at `https://admired-mink-447.convex.cloud`.
14: 
15: Observed failures after Convex deploy:
16: 1. Clerk login with password-created API users can trigger Clerk's new-device email factor, so browser-password sign-in is not deterministic.
17: 2. Deployed Convex initially lacked `seed:seedE2E` / `seed:resetE2EShifts`; deploying fixed that.
18: 3. Geofence tests were stateful/flaky after the first scenario because the same deterministic shift IDs carried cached submitted/success-screen state.
19: 4. Lifecycle test reached coordinator review but could time out on loading/filter state and proof-upload/autosave state.
20: 
21: ## Root-cause analysis
22: 
23: The remaining issue is not missing Clerk credentials anymore. The root causes are:
24: 
25: - E2E fixture reset is not isolated strongly enough for a live Convex/browser run. Resetting the same existing shift documents in place leaves the browser/Convex client able to observe stale details for the same shift IDs after prior test scenarios.
26: - The tests depend on UI-driven geofence settings and role switching in the same page, which adds Clerk/Convex timing races.
27: - The live Clerk flow requires either real email factor handling or backend sign-in tickets for deterministic automation.
28: 
29: ## Possible solutions
30: 
31: ### Solution A: Keep reusing deterministic fixture rows and add waits/reloads
32: 
33: Pros:
34: - Smallest code diff.
35: - No backend fixture changes.
36: 
37: Cons:
38: - Still vulnerable to stale query cache for the same shift IDs.
39: - Requires scattered waits/reloads.
40: - Already showed inconsistent behavior across serial tests.
41: 
42: ### Solution B: Make live E2E fixtures isolated per run/reset
43: 
44: Pros:
45: - Eliminates stale shift-detail cache by creating fresh shift documents for each reset/seed.
46: - Keeps tests representative of the real app while making fixture setup deterministic.
47: - Cleaner root-cause fix than adding waits everywhere.
48: 
49: Cons:
50: - Requires a conservative change in `convex/seed.ts` test fixture helpers and redeploy.
51: 
52: ## Chosen solution
53: 
54: Solution B is the best fix: update E2E seed/reset behavior so each live E2E scenario starts from fresh fixture shift documents, while preserving the existing production app flow. Keep Clerk sign-in tickets for E2E auth only.
55: 
56: ## Implementation stages
57: 
58: ### Stage 1 Ã¢â‚¬â€ Auth determinism
59: 
60: To-do:
61: - Use Clerk Backend API sign-in tickets when `CLERK_SECRET_KEY` is available.
62: - Keep browser password fallback for environments without the secret key.
63: - Clear Clerk session/local storage/cookies between role switches.
64: - Assert E2E credential presence and fail loudly.
65: 
66: ### Stage 2 Ã¢â‚¬â€ Fixture determinism
67: 
68: To-do:
69: - Update `seed:seedE2E` / reset helpers so live E2E resets recreate fixture shifts or otherwise guarantee fresh state.
70: - Ensure geofence settings default off after reset.
71: - Ensure lifecycle and geofence fixture shifts are scheduled/past and assigned to the E2E caregiver.
72: 
73: ### Stage 3 Ã¢â‚¬â€ Test robustness
74: 
75: To-do:
76: - Configure geofence in tests via deployed Convex mutation rather than relying only on UI timing.
77: - Use scoped locators around the target shift card/section.
78: - Add GPS `accuracy` to Playwright geolocation mocks.
79: - Use returned/approved filters explicitly in coordinator review assertions.
80: - Increase Playwright timeout for live Clerk/Convex runs.
81: 
82: ### Stage 4 Ã¢â‚¬â€ Verification
83: 
84: To-do:
85: - Deploy Convex preview with current seed fixes.
86: - Run `npm run lint`.
87: - Run `npm run typecheck`.
88: - Run `npm run test`.
89: - Run full `npm run e2e` until all 9 tests pass.
90: 
91: ## Current status
92: 
93: Stages 1 and parts of Stage 3 were implemented locally. Convex deploy succeeded earlier, but the remaining fixture-isolation change is not complete/deployed yet. Full E2E is still red at the time this doc was written.

CORE RULE: a service is never billed unless its shift documentation is complete and approved (caregiver->coordinator->billing).  import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'
+import { convexTest } from 'convex-test'

+
+const runtimeModules = import.meta.glob('./**/*.*s')
+
+function createRuntimeConvex() {
+  return convexTest({ schema, modules: runtimeModules })
+}
+
+function asAdmin(
+  t: ReturnType<typeof createRuntimeConvex>,
+  adminUserId: string,
+  clerkOrgId: string,
+) {
+  return t.withIdentity({
+    subject: adminUserId,
+    org_id: clerkOrgId,
+    org_role: 'org:admin',
+  })
+}
+
+async function seedTenant(
+  t: ReturnType<typeof createRuntimeConvex>,
+  clerkOrgId: string,
+  adminUserId: string,
+  coordinatorUserId: string,
+  caregiverUserId: string,
+) {
+  return t.run(async (ctx) => {
+    const tenantId = await ctx.db.insert('tenants', {
+      clerkOrgId,
+      name: 'E2E Test Agency',
+      slug: 'e2e-test-agency',
+      createdAt: new Date().toISOString(),
+    })
+
+    const members = [
+      { clerkUserId: adminUserId, role: 'org:admin' as const },
+      { clerkUserId: coordinatorUserId, role: 'org:coordinator' as const },
+      { clerkUserId: caregiverUserId, role: 'org:caregiver' as const },
+    ]
+
+    for (const member of members) {
+      await ctx.db.insert('tenantMembers', {
+        tenantId,
+        clerkUserId: member.clerkUserId,
+        role: member.role,
+        displayName: `E2E ${member.role}`,
+        email: `${member.clerkUserId}@atriax.test`,
+      })
+    }
+
+    return { tenantId }
+  })
+}
+
+async function seedE2E(
+  t: ReturnType<typeof createRuntimeConvex>,
+  clerkOrgId: string,
+  adminUserId: string,
+  coordinatorUserId: string,
+  caregiverUserId: string,
+) {
+  return asAdmin(t, adminUserId, clerkOrgId).mutation(api.seed.seedE2E, {
+    clerkOrgId,
+    adminUserId,
+    coordinatorUserId,
+    caregiverUserId,
+  })
+}
+
+async function resetE2EShifts(
+  t: ReturnType<typeof createRuntimeConvex>,
+  clerkOrgId: string,
+  adminUserId: string,
+  coordinatorUserId: string,
+  caregiverUserId: string,
+) {
+  return asAdmin(t, adminUserId, clerkOrgId).mutation(api.seed.resetE2EShifts, {
+    clerkOrgId,
+    adminUserId,
+    coordinatorUserId,
+    caregiverUserId,
+  })
+}

 567: async function seedE2EFixtures(

 573:

 599:   const memberIds: Record<string, Id<'tenantMembers'>> = {}

 605:       )
 606:       .unique()
 607:     if (existing) {
 608:       memberIds[member.clerkUserId] = existing._id
 609:     } else {
 610:       memberIds[member.clerkUserId] = await ctx.db.insert('tenantMembers', {
 611:         tenantId,
 612:         clerkUserId: member.clerkUserId,
 613:         role: member.role,
 614:         displayName: member.displayName,
 615:         email: member.email,
 616:       })
 617:     }
 618:   }
 619: 
 620:   const findClient = async (displayName: string) => {
 621:     const all = await ctx.db
 622:       .query('clients')
 623:       .withIndex('by_tenant', (q) => q.eq('tenantId', tenantId))
 624:       .collect()
 625:     return all.find((c) => c.displayName === displayName) ?? null
 626:   }
 627: 
 628:   let lifecycleClientId: Id<'clients'>
 629:   const lifecycleClient = await findClient('Sam Lee')
 630:   if (!lifecycleClient) {
 631:     lifecycleClientId = await ctx.db.insert('clients', {
 632:       tenantId,
 633:       displayName: 'Sam Lee',
 634:       serviceType: 'ILS',
 635:       authorizationHours: 30,
 636:       riskFlags: [],
 637:     })
 638:   } else {
 639:     lifecycleClientId = lifecycleClient._id
 640:   }
 641: 
 642:   let geofenceClientId: Id<'clients'>
 643:   const geofenceClient = await findClient('Maya Torres')
 644:   if (!geofenceClient) {
 645:     geofenceClientId = await ctx.db.insert('clients', {
 646:       tenantId,
 647:       displayName: 'Maya Torres',
 648:       serviceType: 'SLS',
 649:       authorizationHours: 40,
 650:       riskFlags: ['mobility'],
 651:       serviceAddress: {
 652:         line1: '123 Hennepin Ave',
 653:         city: 'Minneapolis',
 654:         state: 'MN',
 655:         postalCode: '55401',
 656:         latitude: 44.9778,
 657:         longitude: -93.265,
 658:       },
 659:     })
 660:   } else {
 661:     geofenceClientId = geofenceClient._id
 662:   }
 663: 
 664:   // Reset geofence to disabled so lifecycle tests never prompt for location.
 665:   const existingSettings = await ctx.db
 666:     .query('tenantSettings')
 667:     .withIndex('by_tenant', (q) => q.eq('tenantId', tenantId))
 668:     .unique()
 669:   if (existingSettings) {
 670:     await ctx.db.patch(existingSettings._id, {
 671:       shiftGeofence: DEFAULT_SHIFT_GEOFENCE,
 672:     })
 673:   } else {
 674:     await ctx.db.insert('tenantSettings', {
 675:       tenantId,
 676:       shiftGeofence: DEFAULT_SHIFT_GEOFENCE,
 677:     })
 678:   }
 679: 
 680:   const findShiftsByStart = async (scheduledStart: string) => {
 681:     const all = await ctx.db
 682:       .query('shifts')
 683:       .withIndex('by_tenant_status_start', (q) => q.eq('tenantId', tenantId))
 684:       .collect()
 685:     return all.filter((s) => s.scheduledStart === scheduledStart)
 686:   }
 687: 
 688:   const createCleanShift = async (
 689:     clientId: Id<'clients'>,
 690:     scheduledStart: string,
 691:     scheduledEnd: string,
 692:     serviceType: 'ILS' | 'SLS',
 693:     rate: number,
 694:   ): Promise<Id<'shifts'>> => {
 695:     const shiftId = await ctx.db.insert('shifts', {
 696:       tenantId,
 697:       clientId,
 698:       caregiverId: userIds.caregiverUserId,
 699:       scheduledStart,
 700:       scheduledEnd,
 701:       status: 'scheduled',
 702:       serviceType,
 703:       rate,
 704:     })
 705: 
 706:     await ctx.db.insert('progressNotes', {
 707:       tenantId,
 708:       shiftId,
 709:       startTime: '',
 710:       endTime: '',
 711:       servicesProvided: '',
 712:       clientResponse: '',
 713:       narrative: '',
 714:     })
 715: 
 716:     await ctx.db.insert('shiftTasks', {
 717:       tenantId,
 718:       shiftId,
 719:       title: 'Upload shift documentation proof',
 720:       requiredProof: true,
 721:       status: 'pending',
 722:     })
 723: 
 724:     return shiftId
 725:   }
 726: 
 727:   // Destroy any existing fixture shifts for the known start times so that each
 728:   // E2E reset creates fresh documents with new IDs. This prevents the
 729:   // React/Convex client from reusing stale query/component state keyed by the
 730:   // same shift ID across serial scenarios.
 731:   const lifecycleStart = `${fixtureDate}T09:00:00Z`
 732:   const existingLifecycleShifts = await findShiftsByStart(lifecycleStart)
 733:   for (const shift of existingLifecycleShifts) {
 734:     await deleteShiftChildren(ctx, tenantId, shift._id)
 735:     await ctx.db.delete(shift._id)
 736:   }
 737: 
 738:   const geofenceStart = `${fixtureDate}T14:00:00Z`
 739:   const existingGeofenceShifts = await findShiftsByStart(geofenceStart)
 740:   for (const shift of existingGeofenceShifts) {
 741:     await deleteShiftChildren(ctx, tenantId, shift._id)
 742:     await ctx.db.delete(shift._id)
 743:   }
 744: 
 745:   const lifecycleShiftId = await createCleanShift(
 746:     lifecycleClientId,
 747:     lifecycleStart,
 748:     `${fixtureDate}T13:00:00Z`,
 749:     'ILS',
 750:     30,
 751:   )
 752: 
 753:   const geofenceShiftId = await createCleanShift(
 754:     geofenceClientId,
 755:     geofenceStart,
 756:     `${fixtureDate}T18:00:00Z`,
 757:     'SLS',
 758:     28.5,
 759:   )
 760: 
 761:   return {
 762:     tenantId,
 763:     memberIds,
 764:     lifecycleShiftId,
 765:     geofenceShiftId,
 766:   }
 767: }

 769: // Deterministic E2E fixtures. Each call deletes the existing fixture shifts
 770: // and inserts fresh ones, so serial E2E scenarios never reuse stale shift IDs.
 771: // Geofence is disabled by default so the lifecycle flow can run without
 772: // location. A second client with coordinates is provided for geofence scenarios.
 773: export const seedE2E = mutation({
 774:   args: {
 775:     clerkOrgId: v.string(),
 776:     adminUserId: v.string(),
 777:     coordinatorUserId: v.string(),
 778:     caregiverUserId: v.string(),
 779:   },
 780:   handler: async (ctx, args) => {
 781:     const result = await seedE2EFixtures(ctx, args.clerkOrgId, {
 782:       adminUserId: args.adminUserId,
 783:       coordinatorUserId: args.coordinatorUserId,
 784:       caregiverUserId: args.caregiverUserId,
 785:     })
 786: 
 787:     return {
 788:       status: 'seeded' as const,
 789:       ...result,
 790:     }
 791:   },
 792: })
 793: 
 794: // Resets the E2E fixture shifts back to a clean scheduled state by recreating
 795: // them with fresh IDs and disabling geofence. Used between serial e2e scenarios
 796: // so each test starts from an isolated fixture baseline.
 797: export const resetE2EShifts = mutation({
 798:   args: {
 799:     clerkOrgId: v.string(),
 800:     adminUserId: v.string(),
 801:     coordinatorUserId: v.string(),
 802:     caregiverUserId: v.string(),
 803:   },
 804:   handler: async (ctx, args) => {
 805:     const result = await seedE2EFixtures(ctx, args.clerkOrgId, {
 806:       adminUserId: args.adminUserId,
 807:       coordinatorUserId: args.coordinatorUserId,
 808:       caregiverUserId: args.caregiverUserId,
 809:     })
 810: 
 811:     return {
 812:       status: 'reset' as const,
 813:       ...result,
 814:     }
 815:   },
 816: })

  78:   if (!user) {

 204:   await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')
 205: 
 206:   await selectOrgIfAsked(page, orgId)

 209: export async function signOut(page: Page) {
 210:   // Clear Clerk session state so the next sign-in starts fresh.
 211:   try {
 212:     await page.evaluate(() => {
 213:       localStorage.clear()
 214:       sessionStorage.clear()
 215:     })
 216:   } catch {
 217:     // Some contexts (e.g. about:blank or sandboxed frames) deny storage access.
 218:   }
 219:   await page.context().clearCookies()
 220:   await page.goto('/sign-in')
 221:   await page.waitForLoadState('networkidle')
 222: }
 223: 
 224: async function extractClerkToken(page: Page): Promise<string | null> {
 225:   return page.evaluate(async () => {
 226:     const clerk = (window as unknown as Record<string, unknown>).Clerk as
 227:       | { session?: { getToken: () => Promise<string | null> } }
 228:       | undefined
 229:     const sessionToken = await clerk?.session?.getToken()
 230:     if (sessionToken) return sessionToken
 231: 
 232:     const keys = ['__clerk_client_jwt', '__session', '__clerk_session_jwt']
 233:     for (const key of keys) {
 234:       const value = localStorage.getItem(key)
 235:       if (value) return value
 236:     }
 237:     return null
 238:   })
 239: }
 240: 
 241: export async function resetE2EShifts(page: Page) {
 242:   assertE2ECredentialsConfigured()
 243: 
 244:   // Ensure a clean session before signing in as admin; the caller may still be
 245:   // signed in as a caregiver or coordinator.
 246:   await signOut(page)
 247:   await signInWithClerk(page, E2E_ADMIN_EMAIL, E2E_ADMIN_PASSWORD, E2E_ORG_ID)
 248: 
 249:   const convexUrl = process.env.VITE_CONVEX_URL
 250:   if (!convexUrl) {
 251:     throw new Error('VITE_CONVEX_URL is not set; cannot reset e2e fixtures.')
 252:   }
 253: 
 254:   const token = await extractClerkToken(page)
 255:   if (!token) {
 256:     throw new Error('Could not extract Clerk session token; cannot reset e2e fixtures.')
 257:   }
 258: 
 259:   const response = await fetch(`${convexUrl}/api/mutation`, {
 260:     method: 'POST',
 261:     headers: {
 262:       'Content-Type': 'application/json',
 263:       Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
 264:     },
 265:     body: JSON.stringify({
 266:       path: 'seed:resetE2EShifts',
 267:       args: {
 268:         clerkOrgId: E2E_ORG_ID,
 269:         adminUserId: await findClerkUserId(E2E_ADMIN_EMAIL),
 270:         coordinatorUserId: await findClerkUserId(E2E_COORDINATOR_EMAIL),
 271:         caregiverUserId: await findClerkUserId(E2E_CAREGIVER_EMAIL),
 272:       },
 273:       format: 'json',
 274:     }),
 275:   })
 276: 
 277:   if (!response.ok) {
 278:     const text = await response.text()
 279:     throw new Error(`resetE2EShifts failed: ${response.status} ${text}`)
 280:   }
 281: 
 282:   const result = await response.json()
 283:   console.log('resetE2EShifts result:', result)
 284:   if (result.status !== 'success') {
 285:     throw new Error(`resetE2EShifts failed: ${JSON.stringify(result)}`)
 286:   }
 287: 
 288:   await signOut(page)
 289: }

The recorded Session 8 final gate failed at `.hermes-pipeline/20260626_161701/gate_final_e2e.log:14` and `:18` because the real geofence and lifecycle tests failed before running due missing Clerk E2E credentials. The current `package.json:13` now loads `.env.local`, but I could not verify it here because this sandbox blocks Node child-process spawning (`spawn EPERM`), which prevents Playwright from launching. Run `npm run e2e` in an environment that can spawn Playwright and has the E2E Clerk/Convex credentials loaded, and require a clean pass before committing/landing Phase 1.

.hermes-pipeline\20260626_210401\review_codex_iter4.log:15486:.hermes-pipeline\20260624_161802\review_codex_iter2.md:1270:.hermes-pipeline\20260624_161335\review_codex_iter2.md:1543:  Need final line maybe "VERDICT: CHANGES_ADDRESSED / GREEN"? The prompt required final result as plan/review/summary. The reviewer required final line exactly one of VERDICT: APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED. Since we are the fixer, not reviewer, maybe final message can be summary and state all gates green. We can include "VERDICT: GREEN" maybe. But the prompt says "Output your final result (plan / review / summary) as your last message." It doesn't require exact VERDICT. However to be safe, maybe include "STATUS: GREEN" or "VERDICT: APPROVED"? Since we addressed blockers and gates pass, we can say "SESSION GREEN". The original reviewer's final line must be exactly one of those, but we are not the reviewer. Still, maybe include "VERDICT: CHANGES_ADDRESSED_AND_GREEN". Better not confuse. The final message should be a summary.

The prompt required final result as plan/review/summary. The reviewer required final line exactly one of VERDICT: APPROVED or CHANGES_REQUESTED. Since we are the fixer, not reviewer, maybe final message can be summary and state all gates green. We can include "VERDICT: GREEN" maybe. But the prompt says "Output your final result (plan / review / summary) as your last message." It doesn't require exact VERDICT. However to be safe, maybe include "STATUS: GREEN" or "VERDICT: APPROVED"? Since we addressed blockers and gates pass, we can say "SESSION GREEN". The original reviewer's final line must be exactly one of those, but we are not the reviewer. Still, maybe include "VERDICT: CHANGES_ADDRESSED_AND_GREEN". Better not confuse. The final message should be a summary.

So if I make it fail fast, the gate will fail unless credentials are configured.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_210401\fix_iter1.log:49:  The simpler interpretation: the reviewer is saying the dry-run mode is not acceptable. So we should remove it and require credentials (fail fast). This is what the plan intended: "Playwright e2e (npm run e2e) for the full loop against seeded data". The dry-run was a workaround. 
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_210401\fix_iter1.log:57:  But wait - what about the existing tests that might be run by the pipeline? If I make e2e fail fast, then `npm run e2e` will fail unless credentials are set. The prompt says "Run focused tests/typechecks for touched files/packages. The outer pipeline will run the broad gates after you finish". So the outer pipeline might run `npm run e2e` and fail. But that's the correct behavior per the reviewer.
.hermes-pipeline\20260626_210401\fix_iter1.log:160:  Actually, I should be careful. The reviewer said "Either require credentials and fail fast, or provide a production-app test harness". .hermes-pipeline\20260626_161701\summary.json:3:  "task": "ATRIA-X Phase 1 SESSION 8 \u2014 E2E + ADP contract tests + plug-and-play dry run.\n\nMANDATORY EXECUTION CONSTRAINTS:\n- Do not use Opus/Claude. Use Codex for plan and review, Kimi for implementation/fix as configured by the pipeline.\n- Keep changes conservative and minimalistic. Respect the existing project structure and design.\n- If unsure about code or files, open them. Do not hallucinate.\n- Style: single quotes, no semicolons, 2-space indentation.\n- Follow ATRIA-X rules: tenant access through authHelpers; never bill a shift until documentation is complete and approved; run Convex codegen after Convex API/schema changes.\n- Optimize the flow for speed only where quality is not reduced: do not skip required gates.\n- Create a detailed design/staging document artifact for this session (prefer the pipeline run directory, e.g. design-doc.md / implementation-plan.md; if versioning a docs file in repo is necessary, do it through the pipeline only). The doc must divide the implementation into stages and include a detailed to-do list for each stage before implementation.\n\nTASK:\nImplement/verify ATRIA-X Phase 1 end-to-end and integration test coverage.\n\n(1) Playwright e2e for the full lifecycle against seeded data with geofence disabled:\n- Command target: npm run e2e.\n- Flow: caregiver logs in, opens assigned shift, Clock In, completes the 6-step note.\n- Verify Clock Out is disabled until the note is complete, then enabled.\n- Clock Out -> shift submitted.\n- Coordinator logs in, sees it in the review queue, opens detail, requests a correction.\n- Caregiver fixes + resubmits.\n- Coordinator approves -> shift becomes billing-ready.\n- Assert status = color + word at each step.\n\n(2) Playwright/logic coverage for geofence enabled:\n- Mock browser geolocation inside radius => Clock In/Out allowed and location evidence stored.\n- Mock outside radius => UI shows the Figma-style blocked state and server rejects.\n- Deny geolocation permission => UI shows blocked state and no punch is created.\n- Disable the setting as admin/coordinator => location is no longer requested.\n\n(3) ADP contract/integration tests using the mock adapter:\n- Unconfigured tenant -> clock-in/out succeed and timePunches are marked pending_credentials; app remains fully usable.\n- Flip integrationConnections.status to configured with mock creds and run sync engine -> queued punches post exactly once (idempotent), adpPunchId stored, statuses go synced.\n- Run adpInitialWorkerLoad -> existing profiles matched by email, new ones created with adpAssociateOid.\n- createCaregiver enqueues a worker sync that drains to synced.\n- Assert NO secret values or raw ADP credentials appear in integrationEvents/logs.\n- Assert location evidence is NOT included in ADP punch payloads unless ADP explicitly requires it later.\n\nSeed/fixtures:\n- Update seed.ts if needed for e2e fixtures, idempotently.\n- Prefer deterministic seeded users/roles/shifts/settings.\n\nRequired gates for this session:\n- codegen if Convex API/schema changed\n- npm run lint\n- npm run typecheck\n- npm run test\n- npm run e2e\nAll required gates must be genuinely green before reporting success. Report real pass/fail for each gate in summary.md.",

// Deterministic E2E fixtures. Idempotent by clerkOrgId, member user id, and
// scheduled start time. Geofence is disabled by default so the lifecycle
// flow can run without location. A second client with coordinates is provided
// for geofence scenarios.
export const seedE2E = mutation({
  args: {
    clerkOrgId: v.string(),
    adminUserId: v.string(),
    coordinatorUserId: v.string(),
    caregiverUserId: v.string(),
  },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    const { tenantId } = await requireTenantRole(ctx, args.clerkOrgId, [
      'org:admin',
    ])

    // Fixed fixture date so seeded shifts are always in the past and clock-in is
    // allowed regardless of the actual UTC time the tests run.
    const fixtureDate = REF_TODAY

    const members = [
      {
        clerkUserId: args.adminUserId,
        role: 'org:admin' as const,
        displayName: 'E2E Admin',
        email: 'e2e-admin@atriax.test',
      },
      {
        clerkUserId: args.coordinatorUserId,
        role: 'org:coordinator' as const,
        displayName: 'E2E Coordinator',
        email: 'e2e-coordinator@atriax.test',
      },
      {
        clerkUserId: args.caregiverUserId,
        role: 'org:caregiver' as const,
        displayName: 'E2E Caregiver',
        email: 'e2e-caregiver@atriax.test',
      },
    ]

    const memberIds: Record<string, Id<'tenantMembers'>> = {}
    for (const member of members) {
      const existing = await ctx.db
        .query('tenantMembers')
        .withIndex('by_tenant_user', (q) =>
          q.eq('tenantId', tenantId).eq('clerkUserId', member.clerkUserId),
        )
        .unique()
      if (existing) {
        memberIds[member.clerkUserId] = existing._id
      } else {
        memberIds[member.clerkUserId] = await ctx.db.insert('tenantMembers', {
          tenantId,
          clerkUserId: member.clerkUserId,
          role: member.role,
          displayName: member.displayName,
          email: member.email,
        })
      }
    }

    const findClient = async (displayName: string) => {
      const all = await ctx.db
        .query('clients')
        .withIndex('by_tenant', (q) => q.eq('tenantId', tenantId))
        .collect()
      return all.find((c) => c.displayName === displayName) ?? null
    }

    let lifecycleClientId: Id<'clients'>
    const lifecycleClient = await findClient('Sam Lee')
    if (!lifecycleClient) {
      lifecycleClientId = await ctx.db.insert('clients', {
        tenantId,
        displayName: 'Sam Lee',
        serviceType: 'ILS',
        authorizationHours: 30,
        riskFlags: [],
      })
    } else {
      lifecycleClientId = lifecycleClient._id
    }

    let geofenceClientId: Id<'clients'>
    const geofenceClient = await findClient('Maya Torres')
    if (!geofenceClient) {
      geofenceClientId = await ctx.db.insert('clients', {
        tenantId,
        displayName: 'Maya Torres',
        serviceType: 'SLS',
        authorizationHours: 40,
        riskFlags: ['mobility'],
        serviceAddress: {
          line1: '123 Hennepin Ave',
          city: 'Minneapolis',
          state: 'MN',
          postalCode: '55401',
          latitude: 44.9778,
          longitude: -93.265,
        },
      })
    } else {
      geofenceClientId = geofenceClient._id
    }

    // Reset geofence to disabled so lifecycle tests never prompt for location.
    const existingSettings = await ctx.db
      .query('tenantSettings')
      .withIndex('by_tenant', (q) => q.eq('tenantId', tenantId))
      .unique()
    if (existingSettings) {
      await ctx.db.patch(existingSettings._id, { shiftGeofence: DEFAULT_SHIFT_GEOFENCE })
    } else {
      await ctx.db.insert('tenantSettings', {
        tenantId,
        shiftGeofence: DEFAULT_SHIFT_GEOFENCE,
      })
    }

    const findShift = async (scheduledStart: string) => {
      const all = await ctx.db
        .query('shifts')
        .withIndex('by_tenant_status_start', (q) => q.eq('tenantId', tenantId))
        .collect()
      return all.find((s) => s.scheduledStart === scheduledStart) ?? null
    }

    const resetShift = async (shiftId: Id<'shifts'>) => {
      await ctx.db.patch(shiftId, {
        status: 'scheduled',
        clockInAt: undefined,
        clockOutAt: undefined,
        serviceLocationOverride: undefined,
      })

      const existingNote = await ctx.db
        .query('progressNotes')
        .withIndex('by_tenant_shift', (q) =>
          q.eq('tenantId', tenantId).eq('shiftId', shiftId),
        )
        .unique()
      if (existingNote) {
        await ctx.db.patch(existingNote._id, {
          startTime: '',
          endTime: '',
          servicesProvided: '',
          clientResponse: '',
          narrative: '',
          submittedBy: undefined,
          submittedAt: undefined,
        })
      } else {
        await ctx.db.insert('progressNotes', {
          tenantId,
          shiftId,
          startTime: '',
          endTime: '',
          servicesProvided: '',
          clientResponse: '',
          narrative: '',
        })
      }

      const existingTasks = await ctx.db
        .query('shiftTasks')
        .withIndex('by_tenant_shift', (q) =>
          q.eq('tenantId', tenantId).eq('shiftId', shiftId),
        )
        .collect()
      for (const task of existingTasks) {
        await ctx.db.delete(task._id)
      }
      await ctx.db.insert('shiftTasks', {
        tenantId,
        shiftId,
        title: 'Upload shift documentation proof',
        requiredProof: true,
        status: 'pending',
      })

      const reviews = await ctx.db
        .query('reviewEvents')
        .withIndex('by_tenant_shift', (q) =>
          q.eq('tenantId', tenantId).eq('shiftId', shiftId),
        )
        .collect()
      for (const review of reviews) {
        await ctx.db.delete(review._id)
      }

      const billingLines = await ctx.db
        .query('billingLines')
        .withIndex('by_tenant_shift', (q) =>
          q.eq('tenantId', tenantId).eq('shiftId', shiftId),
        )
        .collect()
      for (const line of billingLines) {
        await ctx.db.delete(line._id)
      }

      const punches = await ctx.db
        .query('timePunches')
        .withIndex('by_tenant_shift', (q) =>
          q.eq('tenantId', tenantId).eq('shiftId', shiftId),
        )
        .collect()
      for (const punch of punches) {
        await ctx.db.delete(punch._id)
      }
    }

    let lifecycleShiftId: Id<'shifts'>
    const lifecycleStart = `${fixtureDate}T09:00:00Z`
    const lifecycleShift = await findShift(lifecycleStart)
    if (!lifecycleShift) {
      lifecycleShiftId = await ctx.db.insert('shifts', {
        tenantId,
        clientId: lifecycleClientId,
        caregiverId: args.caregiverUserId,
        scheduledStart: lifecycleStart,
        scheduledEnd: `${fixtureDate}T13:00:00Z`,
        status: 'scheduled',
        serviceType: 'ILS',
        rate: 30,
      })
    } else {
      lifecycleShiftId = lifecycleShift._id
      await ctx.db.patch(lifecycleShiftId, { caregiverId: args.caregiverUserId })
    }
    await resetShift(lifecycleShiftId)

    let geofenceShiftId: Id<'shifts'>
    const geofenceStart = `${fixtureDate}T14:00:00Z`
    const geofenceShift = await findShift(geofenceStart)
    if (!geofenceShift) {
      geofenceShiftId = await ctx.db.insert('shifts', {
        tenantId,
        clientId: geofenceClientId,
        caregiverId: args.caregiverUserId,
        scheduledStart: geofenceStart,
        scheduledEnd: `${fixtureDate}T18:00:00Z`,
        status: 'scheduled',
        serviceType: 'SLS',
        rate: 28.5,
      })
    } else {
      geofenceShiftId = geofenceShift._id
      await ctx.db.patch(geofenceShiftId, { caregiverId: args.caregiverUserId })
    }
    await resetShift(geofenceShiftId)

    return {
      status: 'seeded' as const,
      tenantId,
      memberIds,
      lifecycleShiftId,
      geofenceShiftId,
    }
  },
})

// Resets the two deterministic E2E fixture shifts back to a clean scheduled
// state and disables geofence. Used between serial e2e scenarios so each test
// starts from the same fixture baseline.
export const resetE2EShifts = mutation({
  args: {
    clerkOrgId: v.string(),
  },
  handler: async (ctx, args) => {
    const { tenantId } = await requireTenantRole(ctx, args.clerkOrgId, [
      'org:admin',
    ])

    // Use the same fixed fixture date as seedE2E so reset finds the rows.
    const fixtureDate = REF_TODAY

    const existingSettings = await ctx.db
      .query('tenantSettings')
      .withIndex('by_tenant', (q) => q.eq('tenantId', tenantId))
      .unique()
    if (existingSettings) {
      await ctx.db.patch(existingSettings._id, { shiftGeofence: DEFAULT_SHIFT_GEOFENCE })
    }

    const findShift = async (scheduledStart: string) => {
      const all = await ctx.db
        .query('shifts')
        .withIndex('by_tenant_status_start', (q) => q.eq('tenantId', tenantId))
        .collect()
      return all.find((s) => s.scheduledStart === scheduledStart) ?? null
    }

    const resetShift = async (shiftId: Id<'shifts'>) => {
      await ctx.db.patch(shiftId, {
        status: 'scheduled',
        clockInAt: undefined,
        clockOutAt: undefined,
        serviceLocationOverride: undefined,
      })

      const existingNote = await ctx.db
        .query('progressNotes')
        .withIndex('by_tenant_shift', (q) =>
          q.eq('tenantId', tenantId).eq('shiftId', shiftId),
        )
        .unique()
      if (existingNote) {
        await ctx.db.patch(existingNote._id, {
          startTime: '',
          endTime: '',
          servicesProvided: '',
          clientResponse: '',
          narrative: '',
          submittedBy: undefined,
          submittedAt: undefined,
        })
      }

      const existingTasks = await ctx.db
        .query('shiftTasks')
        .withIndex('by_tenant_shift', (q) =>
          q.eq('tenantId', tenantId).eq('shiftId', shiftId),
        )
        .collect()
      for (const task of existingTasks) {
        await ctx.db.delete(task._id)
      }
      await ctx.db.insert('shiftTasks', {
        tenantId,
        shiftId,
        title: 'Upload shift documentation proof',
        requiredProof: true,
        status: 'pending',
      })

      const reviews = await ctx.db
        .query('reviewEvents')
        .withIndex('by_tenant_shift', (q) =>
          q.eq('tenantId', tenantId).eq('shiftId', shiftId),
        )
        .collect()
      for (const review of reviews) {
        await ctx.db.delete(review._id)
      }

      const billingLines = await ctx.db
        .query('billingLines')
        .withIndex('by_tenant_shift', (q) =>
          q.eq('tenantId', tenantId).eq('shiftId', shiftId),
        )
        .collect()
      for (const line of billingLines) {
        await ctx.db.delete(line._id)
      }

      const punches = await ctx.db
        .query('timePunches')
        .withIndex('by_tenant_shift', (q) =>
          q.eq('tenantId', tenantId).eq('shiftId', shiftId),
        )
        .collect()
      for (const punch of punches) {
        await ctx.db.delete(punch._id)
      }
    }

    const lifecycleShift = await findShift(`${fixtureDate}T09:00:00Z`)
    if (lifecycleShift) {
      await resetShift(lifecycleShift._id)
    }

    const geofenceShift = await findShift(`${fixtureDate}T14:00:00Z`)
    if (geofenceShift) {
      await resetShift(geofenceShift._id)
    }

    return {
      status: 'reset' as const,
      lifecycleShiftId: lifecycleShift?._id ?? null,
      geofenceShiftId: geofenceShift?._id ?? null,
    }
  },
})

commit d8bd5e0d9fda68a0408d6f89666d07caf7d5dbfc
Author: Diego Molina Sieiro <diego.molina.sieiro@gmail.com>
Date:   Fri Jun 26 23:49:12 2026 -0600

    Fix live Phase 1 E2E fixture isolation


codex
**Findings**

1. Required: narrow the E2E fixture deletion scope. [convex/seed.ts](C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/seed.ts:680) finds shifts only by `scheduledStart`, then [convex/seed.ts](C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/seed.ts:733) deletes every tenant shift at `2024-01-15T09:00:00Z` and [convex/seed.ts](C:/Users/pinol/Documents/Work/atriax/solid-pancake/convex/seed.ts:740) deletes every tenant shift at `2024-01-15T14:00:00Z`. Because `deleteShiftChildren` also deletes billing lines, punches, notes, tasks, and reviews, this public admin mutation can destroy non-E2E tenant data that happens to share those fixed times. Restrict deletion to the intended Sam Lee / Maya Torres fixture shifts, ideally by client + caregiver + fixture marker/known E2E user IDs, and add a regression test proving unrelated same-start shifts and billing lines survive.

Security/auth review: tenant auth guards are present, but the destructive scope above is a concrete tenant data/money risk.

Verification: latest recorded gates show lint/typecheck/unit passing, and `convex/seed.test.ts` passes locally. My local `npm run e2e` attempt failed before tests ran because this sandbox cannot spawn Playwright Chromium (`spawn EPERM`), so I did not count that as an application failure.

VERDICT: CHANGES_REQUESTED
